svg.title: Module 02 one-page guide: The Minimum Viable Agent & a Short History of Agents
svg.text: CSCI 391 · MODULE 02 · ONE-PAGE LECTURE GUIDE
The Minimum Viable Agent & a Short History of
Agents
A system prompt, a set of tools, and a loop — and fifty years of ideas behind them.
Part I · Foundations and Mindset · Week 2 · Read: Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 2
OPENING CASE
“I ordered the blue kettle two weeks ago and it arrived dented. I'd like a refund.” A chatbot apologizes. An agent
looks up the order, checks refund eligibility, issues the refund through a scoped tool, and confirms — choosing each
step from what it observed in the last one.
The toolset defines the agent's blast radius. Each tool should do one narrow
thing, with an explicit schema.
KEY FRAMEWORK
Five-level agent taxonomy
L0 Scripted automation — no LLM required
L1 LLM as a text function
L2 Tool-using LLM
L3 Goal-directed agent with planning
L4 Adaptive agent with persistent memory
L5 Autonomous multi-agent / computer-use systems
YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO
Assemble a Minimum Viable Agent: system prompt,
tools, user message, loop
Classify systems using the five-level taxonomy
Identify the classic pitfalls: LLM-as-ground-truth,
longer-thinking-is-better, tool breadth
Connect modern agents to STRIPS, SHRDLU, expert
systems, the frame problem, and BDI
ENTERPRISE LENS · ADDISON BOYER
Scope tools the way you scope IAM roles: the smallest set of verbs that completes the job. A 'refund' tool should
not also be able to edit orders.
Never treat model output as a system of record. Verify facts against the database, the catalog, or the API that
owns them.
Most problems I've seen ship at Level 1 or 2 and call themselves Level 4. Name the level honestly in your design
doc.
DISCUSS
→ Which level is the system you use most at work or school — honestly?
→ Which problems in modern agents are genuinely new, and which are 1970s problems in new clothes?
Concepts after Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 2. Case framing, synthesis, and enterprise lens: Addison Boyer.
